title: batchMint has no per-mint or cumulative price ceiling; front-runner can bump price between submission and inclusion, gas-griefing the entire batch
description: BatchNFTMinter does not accept a `maxStartingPrice` or `maxCumulativePrice` parameter. The dispatcher's `price` grows by `growthBasisPoints` per mint, so any concurrent mint between an honest user's submission and inclusion makes the cumulative cost exceed the prepaid `paymentAmount`. The whole batch reverts atomically; the caller pays only gas but the batch never completes, while the front-runner secures the cheaper slot.
impact: Caller loses tx gas only. Atomic rollback (documented in NatSpec L26-L27) means the dispatcher cannot pull more than the prepaid `paymentAmount`: if cumulative cost exceeds it, an inner mint reverts and the entire batch unwinds, returning the prepayment to the caller. No principal loss path. The harm is repeated denial of the batch entrypoint when the mempool is contested — a quality-of-service hit, not a value leak.
attackPath: Honest user submits batchMint(count=N, paymentAmount=P) sized for current dispatcher price
Front-runner observes the tx in the mempool and inserts their own mint() before it
Dispatcher price compounds by (1+g/10000); honest user's cumulative cost now exceeds P
Honest user's tx reverts atomically; user pays only gas
Front-runner secured the cheaper slot; honest user must retry with a larger budget
recommendation: Add a `maxCumulativePrice` (or `maxPerMintPrice`) parameter and revert if `nftMinter.configs(dispatcherIndex).price > maxStartingPrice` at the start of the call. A coarse `maxPaymentPerMint` would also bound user downside.
severityRationale: DOWNGRADED from medium to low. C4 treats pure gas-only losses (where principal is fully refunded by atomic rollback) as Low/QA. The recommendation (add a maxStartingPrice / maxCumulativePrice param) is a quality-of-service hardening, not a fix for a value-loss bug. Distinct from a sandwich that actually steals funds — here the protocol's atomic rollback already prevents overpayment. Recommendation goes into the QA report.

classification.likelihood: Plausible on any non-private mempool. Bot competition for the early-minter geometric APY premium is a known incentive on this protocol.
classification.assumptions: Public mempool. growthBasisPoints > 0 (otherwise no per-mint price growth and no griefing surface).

scannerAttribution.dedupNotes: Distinct from DEDUP-003 (which is dispatcher-leg AMM slippage on the Balancer pool). DEDUP-002 is curve-side price growth between blocks; DEDUP-003 is in-block AMM slippage during the swap leg. Different root causes, different mitigations — both kept.

sanitization.notes: Not a known issue. Not addressed by any prior submission. The known-issue 'Price growth via basis points may compound to very large values over many mints (documented design)' is from yield-claim-nft, not nft-staking, and addresses long-term price compounding — not the inability of batchMint callers to set a slippage ceiling. Distinct issue.

metadata.reclassificationReason: Atomic rollback prevents overpayment; loss is gas-only. C4 treats gas-only losses as Low/QA.
